project.title: Payment Processing Engine (Level 2: Requirement Build)

projectBrief.whatAreWeBuilding: A flexible payment checkout engine that processes credit cards, digital wallets, and crypto payments through one clean, standard flow without cluttering the checkout code.
projectBrief.problemItSolves: Online checkouts must support cards, digital wallets, and bank transfers without rewriting the checkout screen every time a new payment option is added.
projectBrief.finishedAppDescription: A robust payment gateway application handling checkout carts. The gateway accepts any valid PaymentMethod implementation, validates payment credentials (card Luhn checksum, UPI virtual payment address, crypto wallet hash), computes method-specific convenience fees, and generates transaction receipts.
javaFundamentals: Polymorphism and runtime dynamic method dispatch
Decoupling checkout logic from payment implementations (Open-Closed Principle in action)
Transaction status models and audit receipt generation
projectBrief.motivatingQuote: Polymorphism lets you write code that doesn't care about what type it's dealing with, as long as it honors the contract.

realWorldScenario.headline: E-Commerce Multi-Gateway Checkout Engine
realWorldScenario.story: A global online retailer processes millions of orders daily. Customers check out using Visa credit cards, instant UPI QR transfers, or Bitcoin/Ethereum crypto wallets. The CheckoutService must process the transaction seamlessly without knowing the low-level mechanics of each payment rail.
realWorldScenario.context: Fintech architectures rely on polymorphic interfaces so that introducing a new payment rail (e.g. Apple Pay, PayPal) requires zero edits to existing checkout code.

functional: Define a PaymentMethod interface with methods: boolean validateCredentials(), double calculateFee(double amount), and boolean processPayment(double amount).
Implement CreditCardPayment supporting 16-digit card number, CVV, expiry date, and charging a 2.5% convenience fee.
Implement UpiPayment supporting virtual payment address format ('user@bank') and charging a flat $0.50 processing fee.
Implement CryptoPayment supporting wallet address format (40+ hex characters) and charging network gas fees.

Implement PaymentGateway class with processOrder(String orderId, double amount, PaymentMethod method) that validates credentials, computes final charged amount, executes payment, and generates a formatted receipt.
Create a driver demonstrating processing various transactions through the same gateway instance without type casting.

All method interactions in the gateway must strictly occur through the PaymentMethod interface reference.

processPayment must return false and abort if validateCredentials() fails.

Choose receipt formatting layout and transaction ID generation style.
Decide whether to support partial refund operations on PaymentMethod.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why is avoiding 'instanceof' and switch statements so important in payment processors?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: If your gateway uses switch(paymentType), every time your company adds a new payment method (like ApplePay), you must open and modify the core PaymentGateway code, violating the Open-Closed Principle and risking regressions in existing payment logic.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What happens under the hood during dynamic dispatch?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: When gateway calls method.processPayment(amount), the JVM inspects the actual object on the Heap at runtime (e.g. CreditCardPayment vs CryptoPayment) and routes execution to that specific class's vtable implementation.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why use an interface instead of an abstract class here?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: An interface specifies a pure capability ('can process payments'). A class implementing PaymentMethod could also extend an AuditEntity or Serializable class. Interfaces allow flexible, multiple-inheritance-like contracts.

boundaryCases: Processing payment of minimum allowable amount ($1.00) -> Fee correctly calculated
Crypto address exactly 42 characters starting with '0x' -> Validation passes
invalidInputCases: Credit Card with 12 digits instead of 16 -> validateCredentials() returns false; transaction REJECTED
UPI ID without '@' symbol (e.g. 'johnbank') -> validateCredentials() returns false; transaction REJECTED
Passing negative order amount (-$50) -> Rejected before processing

# Payment Processing Engine (Java OOP)

## Overview
A decoupled, enterprise-grade payment gateway built in Java demonstrating runtime polymorphism, interface-driven design, and the Open-Closed Principle (OCP).

## Architecture Blueprint
```
                                +---------------------------------+
                                |       <<interface>>             |
                                |       PaymentMethod             |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | + validateCredentials(): boolean|
                                | + calculateFee(amt: double): dbl|
                                | + processPayment(amt: dbl): bool|
                                | + getPaymentType(): String      |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                                 ^
                                                 |
          +--------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
          |                                      |                                      |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
|   CreditCardPayment   |              |      UpiPayment       |              |     CryptoPayment     |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
| - cardNumber: String  |              | - upiId: String       |              | - walletAddress: String|
| - cvv: String         |              +-----------------------+              | - network: String     |
+-----------------------+              | + [implements methods]|              +-----------------------+
| + [implements methods]|              +-----------------------+              | + [implements methods]|
+-----------------------+                                                     +-----------------------+

                                +---------------------------------+
                                |         PaymentGateway          |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | + processOrder(orderId: String, |
                                |     amount: double,             |
                                |     method: PaymentMethod)      |
                                +---------------------------------+
```

## Why Polymorphism Matters Here
`PaymentGateway` interacts exclusively with the `PaymentMethod` interface. It contains **zero** `instanceof` statements and **zero** `if-else` type switches. To introduce a new payment method (e.g. `ApplePayPayment`), developers write one new class without modifying existing gateway code.

## How to Run
```bash
javac PaymentMethod.java CreditCardPayment.java UpiPayment.java CryptoPayment.java PaymentGateway.java PaymentApp.java
java PaymentApp
```

## Sample Receipt Output
```text
=======================================================
                  PAYMENT RECEIPT                      
=======================================================
Transaction ID:   TXN-2026-99014
Order ID:         ORD-8402
Payment Rail:     CREDIT_CARD (Ending in *4412)
Base Amount:      $120.00
Processing Fee:   $3.00 (2.5%)
Total Charged:    $123.00
Status:           AUTHORIZED / PAID
=======================================================
```

project.title: Payment Processing Engine (Level 2: Requirement Build)

projectBrief.whatAreWeBuilding: A flexible payment checkout engine that processes credit cards, digital wallets, and crypto payments through one clean, standard flow without cluttering the checkout code.
projectBrief.problemItSolves: Online checkouts must support cards, digital wallets, and bank transfers without rewriting the checkout screen every time a new payment option is added.
projectBrief.finishedAppDescription: A robust payment gateway application handling checkout carts. The gateway accepts any valid PaymentMethod implementation, validates payment credentials (card Luhn checksum, UPI virtual payment address, crypto wallet hash), computes method-specific convenience fees, and generates transaction receipts.
javaFundamentals: Polymorphism and runtime dynamic method dispatch
Decoupling checkout logic from payment implementations (Open-Closed Principle in action)
Transaction status models and audit receipt generation
projectBrief.motivatingQuote: Polymorphism lets you write code that doesn't care about what type it's dealing with, as long as it honors the contract.

realWorldScenario.headline: E-Commerce Multi-Gateway Checkout Engine
realWorldScenario.story: A global online retailer processes millions of orders daily. Customers check out using Visa credit cards, instant UPI QR transfers, or Bitcoin/Ethereum crypto wallets. The CheckoutService must process the transaction seamlessly without knowing the low-level mechanics of each payment rail.
realWorldScenario.context: Fintech architectures rely on polymorphic interfaces so that introducing a new payment rail (e.g. Apple Pay, PayPal) requires zero edits to existing checkout code.

functional: Define a PaymentMethod interface with methods: boolean validateCredentials(), double calculateFee(double amount), and boolean processPayment(double amount).
Implement CreditCardPayment supporting 16-digit card number, CVV, expiry date, and charging a 2.5% convenience fee.
Implement UpiPayment supporting virtual payment address format ('user@bank') and charging a flat $0.50 processing fee.
Implement CryptoPayment supporting wallet address format (40+ hex characters) and charging network gas fees.

Implement PaymentGateway class with processOrder(String orderId, double amount, PaymentMethod method) that validates credentials, computes final charged amount, executes payment, and generates a formatted receipt.
Create a driver demonstrating processing various transactions through the same gateway instance without type casting.
technicalConstraints: PaymentGateway must NOT contain if-else checks or instanceof checks for specific payment subclasses.
All method interactions in the gateway must strictly occur through the PaymentMethod interface reference.
calculateFee() must always return non-negative fees.
processPayment must return false and abort if validateCredentials() fails.
userDecisions: Decide whether to add simulated network latency or random failure simulation.
Choose receipt formatting layout and transaction ID generation style.
Decide whether to support partial refund operations on PaymentMethod.

inputsRequired: Payment details: card number/CVV, UPI VPA, or Crypto wallet address
outputsRequired: Fee breakdown and total amount charged
Cryptographic transaction hash or reference ID
conditionalLogic: validateCredentials() checks: card length == 16, CVV length == 3, UPI contains '@', Crypto starts with '0x'
Gateway checkout check: if (!method.validateCredentials()) return TransactionResult.failed()
loopStructures: Iteration through an array or queue of checkout orders in Main

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why is avoiding 'instanceof' and switch statements so important in payment processors?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: If your gateway uses switch(paymentType), every time your company adds a new payment method (like ApplePay), you must open and modify the core PaymentGateway code, violating the Open-Closed Principle and risking regressions in existing payment logic.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What happens under the hood during dynamic dispatch?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: When gateway calls method.processPayment(amount), the JVM inspects the actual object on the Heap at runtime (e.g. CreditCardPayment vs CryptoPayment) and routes execution to that specific class's vtable implementation.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why use an interface instead of an abstract class here?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: An interface specifies a pure capability ('can process payments'). A class implementing PaymentMethod could also extend an AuditEntity or Serializable class. Interfaces allow flexible, multiple-inheritance-like contracts.

hintSystem.level1Conceptual: Accept the interface type as the parameter in the gateway method.

hintSystem.level1Conceptual: Check format rules before authorizing payment.

normalCases: Credit Card on $100 order -> Fee: $2.50 (2.5%), Total Charged: $102.50, Status: APPROVED
UPI on $40 order -> Fee: $0.50 (flat), Total Charged: $40.50, Status: APPROVED
Crypto on $500 order -> Fee: $5.00 (gas fee), Total Charged: $505.00, Status: APPROVED
boundaryCases: Processing payment of minimum allowable amount ($1.00) -> Fee correctly calculated
Crypto address exactly 42 characters starting with '0x' -> Validation passes
invalidInputCases: Credit Card with 12 digits instead of 16 -> validateCredentials() returns false; transaction REJECTED
UPI ID without '@' symbol (e.g. 'johnbank') -> validateCredentials() returns false; transaction REJECTED
Passing negative order amount (-$50) -> Rejected before processing
edgeCases: Adding a brand-new payment type (e.g. GiftCardPayment) without touching a single line of PaymentGateway code

debuggingGuide: Calling concrete methods not in the interface: When programming to an interface, you can only invoke methods declared on PaymentMethod.
NullPointerException on payment method: Always verify method != null at the start of processOrder.
Fee calculation returning 0: Ensure percentage calculations divide by 100.0 (double) rather than integer 100.
instanceof code smells: If you find yourself writing if (method instanceof CreditCardPayment), stop! Move that specialized logic inside the CreditCardPayment class itself.
projectPolish: Mask sensitive card details in receipt output (e.g. '************4412').
Generate unique timestamped transaction reference codes for approved receipts.
Display an ASCII checkout receipt with clear subtotal, fee, and total lines.

# Payment Processing Engine (Java OOP)

## Overview
A decoupled, enterprise-grade payment gateway built in Java demonstrating runtime polymorphism, interface-driven design, and the Open-Closed Principle (OCP).

## Architecture Blueprint
```
                                +---------------------------------+
                                |       <<interface>>             |
                                |       PaymentMethod             |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | + validateCredentials(): boolean|
                                | + calculateFee(amt: double): dbl|
                                | + processPayment(amt: dbl): bool|
                                | + getPaymentType(): String      |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                                 ^
                                                 |
          +--------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
          |                                      |                                      |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
|   CreditCardPayment   |              |      UpiPayment       |              |     CryptoPayment     |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
| - cardNumber: String  |              | - upiId: String       |              | - walletAddress: String|
| - cvv: String         |              +-----------------------+              | - network: String     |
+-----------------------+              | + [implements methods]|              +-----------------------+
| + [implements methods]|              +-----------------------+              | + [implements methods]|
+-----------------------+                                                     +-----------------------+

                                +---------------------------------+
                                |         PaymentGateway          |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | + processOrder(orderId: String, |
                                |     amount: double,             |
                                |     method: PaymentMethod)      |
                                +---------------------------------+
```

## Why Polymorphism Matters Here
`PaymentGateway` interacts exclusively with the `PaymentMethod` interface. It contains **zero** `instanceof` statements and **zero** `if-else` type switches. To introduce a new payment method (e.g. `ApplePayPayment`), developers write one new class without modifying existing gateway code.

## How to Run
```bash
javac PaymentMethod.java CreditCardPayment.java UpiPayment.java CryptoPayment.java PaymentGateway.java PaymentApp.java
java PaymentApp
```

## Sample Receipt Output
```text
=======================================================
                  PAYMENT RECEIPT                      
=======================================================
Transaction ID:   TXN-2026-99014
Order ID:         ORD-8402
Payment Rail:     CREDIT_CARD (Ending in *4412)
Base Amount:      $120.00
Processing Fee:   $3.00 (2.5%)
Total Charged:    $123.00
Status:           AUTHORIZED / PAID
=======================================================
```
